items.title: [Bug] kvcache-watcher drops a cache pod's slot ranges when the pod owns the first and last slot
items.author: hmdsefi
items.body_excerpt:
## 🐛 Describe the bug

`mergeSlots` in `cmd/kvcache-watcher/main.go` has a ring case: when a pod owns slot 0 and the last slot, it returns a single range from the start of the pod's last range to the end of its first range. Every other range of that pod is dropped, and the returned range has `start > end`.

The L2 placement in `aibrix_kvcache` (`BasePlacement.construct_cluster`) reads this metadata for both InfiniStore (`kvcache_nodes`) and HPKV (`hpkv_cluster_metadata`). It expands each range with `range(start, end + 1)`, which is empty for that range. So the pod gets no slots, and all keys go to the other pods.

## Steps to Reproduce

Unit level, with the watcher's defaults of 4096 slots and 100 virtual nodes:

1. Call `calculateSlotDistribution` for two pods named `kvcache-0` and `kvcache-1`.
2. Call `mergeSlots` on each pod's slots.

At df20e52e, `kvcache-1` owns 2046 slots but gets one range, `{start: 4095, end: 1}`. With three pods, `kvcache-2` owns 1438 slots and gets `{start: 4095, end: 0}`.

A smaller case: `mergeSlots([0 1 2 100 101 4094 4095], 4096)` returns `[{4094 2}]`.

## Expected behavior

`[{0 2} {100 101} {4094 4095}]`: every range the pod owns, each with `start <= end`.

## Environment

- AIBrix version: main at df20e52e
- Deployment environment: unit test of cmd/kvcache-watcher
- Cloud provider (if applicable): n/a
- LLM(s) being used: not model specific
- Client library version (if applicable): n/a

## Area

KV Cache

I'd like to fix this. I have a change with tests ready and will open a PR.

items.title: [QST] SM120 FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate, plain form against block-scaled form with unit scales
items.author: emre570
items.body_excerpt:
**What is your question?**

On an RTX 5080, the plain FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate runs at half the rate of the block-scaled FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate. When all scale bytes are `0x7F` (UE8M0 1.0), the two forms give equal bits.

My FP8 attention kernel in CuTe DSL used `MmaFP8Op`. I changed it to `MmaMXF8Op` with constant unit scales and no other change. The kernel time went from 123.6 ms to 83.6 ms and the output is byte-equal (sgl-project/sglang#43390). So a user can do this today. My question is about the default.

1. Is there a reason to keep the plain form for E4M3 x E4M3 with FP32 accumulate on SM120?
2. If there is no reason, do you want `MmaFP8Op` and `rr_op_selector_sm120` to emit the block-scaled form with unit scales for this case? I can send a PR.

### Related report

The same behavior is reported in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5963 for the FlashInfer SM120 FP8 attention kernel, with RTX 5090 numbers and a bit-identity check. That issue also points to the MXFP8 attention work in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3628 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4149. The numbers below add an RTX 5080 and a CUTLASS GEMM measurement to that report.

### Scope

E4M3 x E4M3, FP32 accumulate, one RTX 5080 (driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.3, CUTLASS `ffa119a12`). I did not measure other types or other cards.

### Raw MMA rate

Independent MMA chains, no memory access, 84 SMs. The rate is the same from 4 to 32 warps per SM.

| instruction | TFLOP/s |
|---|---:|
| `kind::f8f6f4.m16n8k32 ... f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` | 246 |
| `kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.scale_vec::1X.m16n8k32 ... f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32.ue8m0` | 489 |

### Bit equality

- Random finite inputs. 0 of 704,643,072 accumulator registers differ.
- Negative control with scale 2.0. 704,643,071 registers differ.
- Edge cases (subnormal, ±448, NaN bytes, accumulator start at zero, FLT_MAX, subnormal, infinity, NaN). 30 classes, 176,160,768 registers each, 0 bits differ.

### CUTLASS GEMM

I used the SM120 `CollectiveBuilder` with `OpClassTensorOp`, pingpong schedule, tile 128x128x128, FP32 output. Then I changed only the instruction in `SM120_16x8x32_TN<float_e4m3_t, float_e4m3_t, float>` to the block-scaled form. The scale `0x7F7F7F7F` stays in a register. There is no scale factor tensor and no additional load. The patch is 34 lines.

I measured 30 shapes from real models. All 30 give 0 different output words. Five examples:

| shape source | M x N x K | plain | patched | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan 2.2 14B, `to_q` | 32760 x 5120 x 5120 | 236.1 | 398.6 | 1.69x |
| Llama 3.3 70B, MLP up | 4096 x 28672 x 8192 | 234.7 | 398.1 | 1.70x |
| FLUX.1-dev, FFN up | 4608 x 12288 x 3072 | 231.8 | 393.3 | 1.70x |
| MiniMax-H3, FFN up | 30272 x 14336 x 5376 | 234.6 | 363.5 | 1.55x |
| Gemma 3 27B, MLP up | 128 x 21504 x 5376 | 195.8 | 203.4 | 1.04x |

TFLOP/s. The speedup is 1.55x to 1.72x for the 22 shapes with M of 4096 or more. It is 1.04x to 1.82x for the 8 shapes with M = 128, where the low end is DRAM-bound.

Nsight Compute on the stock plain kernel shows the tensor pipe 96% busy. The MMA instruction rate is 47.9% of the peak.

One caution. These numbers use `max_swizzle_size = 8`. With the default of 1, three large shapes become DRAM-bound and the patched kernel is slower than the plain kernel (0.88x). I can open a different issue for that with the data.

### Where the plain form is used

- CuTe DSL `MmaFP8Op`
- `rr_op_selector_sm120` in `sm120_mma_builder.inl`, `sm120_array_mma_builder.inl` and `sm120_blockwise_mma_builder.inl`

cuBLASLt on the same card uses `QMMA.SF.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3.E8` in its FP8 GEMM kernel and no plain `QMMA`.

I can share the benchmark source, the patch and the raw results if they are useful.

items.title: Expert Parallelism (EP) roadmap for SM12x b12x MoE kernel (b12x_fused_moe / B12xMoEWrapper)
items.author: ItamarTerem
items.body_excerpt:
Hi flashinfer team,
We're deploying a large MoE model (384 experts, top_k=8) on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120/Blackwell workstation) using the b12x_fused_moe CuteDSL kernel via TensorRT-LLM's pytorch backend, and have hit the Expert Parallelism restriction:

b12x_fused_moe does not yet support Expert Parallelism
(num_local_experts={X} != num_experts={Y}).
Use a different MoE backend for EP configurations.

This comes from the explicit guard in flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py (both in the free function b12x_fused_moe and in B12xMoEWrapper.__init__), confirmed in flashinfer version 0.6.12.
Context on why this matters for us specifically: without EP, every GPU must retain workspace/routing capacity sized for the full state_E (all 384 experts), even though tensor parallelism already shards each expert's weights across GPUs. This is a meaningful, measured memory cost — in our case, the dynamic workspace's packed_input buffer alone accounts for roughly 7–11GB/GPU across a 60-MoE-layer model, purely from having to size for the worst-case "all experts active" scenario rather than a num_experts/ep_size subset.

What we're asking:

1. Is EP support for the SM12x b12x kernel family (static/dynamic/micro backends) on the roadmap, even at a preliminary stage?
2. Is there a rough timeline or tracking issue we could follow?
3. Are there known architectural blockers specific to SM120 (vs. SM100/SM103, where other kernels like MegaMoE already support EP) that make this a harder problem here?

We also note that vLLM's FlashInferB12xExperts (_supports_parallel_config) explicitly declines to use this backend when EP is requested, for the same underlying reason — so this appears to be a shared, cross-framework limitation rather than something specific to our integration.
Happy to provide more detail on our exact shapes/config if useful. Thanks for your work on this — the b12x kernel has otherwise been the only correctness-verified MoE path we've found for SM120 (CUTLASS produces silently incorrect output on this architecture in our testing).

items.title: [Docs][Core/Auth] Document token authentication on by default for all clusters
items.author: MortalHappiness
items.body_excerpt:
Update `doc/source/ray-security/token-auth.md`, `doc/source/core/internals/token-authentication.md` and the VM, Kubernetes and on-prem deployment guides: token auth is on by default for every cluster from 2.61, how nodes and clients get the token, and the `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` opt-out (which every node and client of an opted-out cluster must set).

In the VM deployment guide, note that existing `ray up` clusters update their worker nodes once after upgrading to a Ray version with the auth token file mount (#67050): each worker reruns its setup commands and restarts Ray, and in Docker mode its container restarts. Instances aren't relaunched.

Also document metrics scraping in `doc/source/cluster/metrics.md`. Users who run their own Prometheus with the dashboard's config add `authorization: {type: Bearer, credentials_file: <path to the token file>}` to the `ray` scrape job when auth is on. `ray metrics launch-prometheus` puts the token inline in its own config, `./prometheus-<version>.linux-amd64/ray_prometheus.yml` (mode 0600), when `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set.

Also say in the docs and the release notes that an auth rejection now raises `AuthenticationError` at once, where `ray.init(address=...)` used to raise `ConnectionError` after retrying. `AuthenticationError` subclasses `ConnectionError`, so existing handlers still catch it.

Also document that `ray start --head` needs a token created first with `ray get-auth-token --generate`, and that the token must then be copied to every node.

Also document `RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS=1` in `doc/source/cluster/metrics.md` and `doc/source/ray-security/token-auth.md`. Setting it on every node serves Ray's metrics endpoints without the token, while token auth still protects everything else.

Must land in the same release as #67055.

items.title: [Bug] Batch templates emit arguments rejected by SGLang 0.5.22 and vLLM 0.32.0
items.author: Jackmeson1
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Accepted optional batch settings produce incompatible arguments:

- **SGLang 0.5.22 translation:** `parallelism.pp=2` emits ambiguous `--pp 2`; `engine_args.block_size=16` emits unrecognized `--block-size 16`.
- **vLLM 0.32.0 compatibility:** `engine_args.swap_space=4` emits unrecognized `--swap-space 4`. `quantization.weight=bf16` emits `--quantization bf16`: argparse accepts it, but quantization validation rejects it as an unknown method.

Both baseline argument lists parse. SGLang forwards unmapped typed fields; vLLM emits flags independently of engine.version (`python/aibrix/aibrix/batch/manifest/engine_adapter.py:128,156,228,241`).

Report only; we are not working on a fix.

### Steps to Reproduce

At the AIBrix commit below, with its Python dependencies installed, save as `repro.py` at repository root:

```python
import argparse
import contextlib
import io
import json
import sys
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == "render":
    from aibrix.batch.manifest.engine_adapter import build_engine_args
    from aibrix.batch.template import ModelDeploymentTemplateSpec as Spec

    rows = []
    for engine, version, changes in [
        ("sglang", "0.5.22", [{}, {"parallelism": {"pp": 2}},
                            {"engine_args": {"block_size": 16}}]),
        ("vllm", "0.32.0", [{}, {"engine_args": {"swap_space": 4}},
                          {"quantization": {"weight": "bf16"}}]),
    ]:
        for change in changes:
            spec = Spec.model_validate(dict(
                engine=dict(type=engine, version=version, image=engine),
                model_source=dict(type="huggingface", uri="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B"),
                accelerator=dict(type="H100", count=change.get("parallelism", {}).get("pp", 1)),
                supported_endpoints=["/v1/chat/completions"], **change))
            rows.append([engine, build_engine_args(spec)])
    print(json.dumps(rows))
else:
    if mode == "sglang":
        from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=mode)
        ServerArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
    else:
        from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.cli_args import make_arg_parser
        from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
        from vllm.config.model import ModelConfig
        parser = make_arg_parser(FlexibleArgumentParser(prog=mode))
    for engine, argv in json.load(open("cases.json")):
        if engine != mode:
            continue
        print("argv:", *argv)
        errors = io.StringIO()
        try:
            with contextlib.redirect_stderr(errors):
                parsed = parser.parse_args(argv)
        except SystemExit:
            print(errors.getvalue().splitlines()[-1])
            continue
        print("argparse: ACCEPT")
        if mode == "vllm":
            try:
                ModelConfig._verify_quantization(NS(
                    quantization=parsed.quantization,
                    model_arch_config=NS(quantization_config=None),
                    allow_deprecated_quantization=False))
            except ValueError as error:
                print("later validation:", error)
```

Render:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python/aibrix python repro.py render > cases.json
```

Replay from the same directory in separate Python 3.12 environments:

```sh
# SGLang environment
pip install sglang==0.5.22
python repro.py sglang
# vLLM environment
pip install vllm==0.32.0
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python repro.py vllm
```

### Expected behavior

Accepted template settings produce arguments compatible with the selected engine/version.

### Environment

AIBrix `b389a59a58ea`; Linux CPU; Python 3.10 rendering/3.12 parsers; engine sources verified against tags v0.5.22/v0.32.0. Validation calls the real quantization validator without model initialization. No server launched. The sample pins vLLM 0.6.3; its launch behavior was not tested.

items.title: [Feature] Add DeepInfer as a supported inference engine
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 Feature Description and Motivation

[DeepInfer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer) is DeepSeek's newly open-sourced high-performance inference framework for large-scale DeepSeek model inference.

AIBrix currently supports multiple inference engines, including vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and xLLM. This issue proposes adding DeepInfer as another supported engine.

The integration would allow users to deploy and operate DeepInfer workloads through AIBrix and use AIBrix for Kubernetes orchestration, request routing, autoscaling, observability, and, where the engine contracts permit, KV-cache and disaggregated inference management.

DeepInfer currently provides offline inference and explicitly lists several components required for a complete online inference service as not yet included:

- KV-cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation
- Load balancing across data-parallel prefill and decode replicas

Because an online serving API and metrics contract are not yet available, the integration should be developed incrementally as those interfaces become stable.

### Use Case

Users serving DeepSeek models on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs or Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs may want to use DeepInfer's optimized kernels, scheduling, parallelism, and deterministic inference capabilities while relying on AIBrix for the Kubernetes control plane.

A target deployment should eventually support:

- Declaring `model.aibrix.ai/engine: deepinfer`
- Deploying DeepInfer workers using Deployment or StormService
- Routing inference requests through AIBrix Gateway
- Discovering ready DeepInfer replicas
- Mapping DeepInfer metrics to AIBrix's engine-neutral metrics
- Applying supported routing and autoscaling policies
- Providing a documented example for a DeepInfer-supported DeepSeek model

### Proposed Solution

Implement the integration in stages.

#### Phase 1: Define the serving contract

Coordinate with the DeepInfer project and document the interfaces required by AIBrix:

- Online inference API and streaming behavior
- Model-name and error-response semantics
- Health and readiness endpoints
- Prometheus metrics endpoint and metric names
- Container image and startup configuration
- Prefill/decode role and transfer metadata, when available

The initial integration should not assume that DeepInfer is OpenAI-compatible until that contract is provided and verified.

#### Phase 2: Basic AIBrix engine support

Once DeepInfer provides an online serving interface:

- Add `deepinfer` as a supported value of `model.aibrix.ai/engine`
- Add the available metric mappings
- Support pod discovery, health checking, and ordinary gateway routing
- Add a sample deployment for supported hardware and models
- Add integration tests covering request forwarding and failure propagation
- Document supported and unsupported AIBrix routing policies

Gateway-tracked routing policies may be enabled before engine-metric-based policies when the required metrics are unavailable.

#### Phase 3: Advanced integration

Track advanced capabilities separately as their DeepInfer contracts stabilize:

- KV-cache-aware routing
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation
- Independent scaling of data-parallel prefill and decode replicas
- DeepInfer-specific runtime management
- NVIDIA and Ascend deployment validation

### Initial Completion Criteria

- [ ] A stable DeepInfer online serving contract is documented
- [ ] `model.aibrix.ai/engine: deepinfer` is recognized
- [ ] AIBrix Gateway can route requests to DeepInfer replicas
- [ ] Health/readiness and supported metrics are integrated
- [ ] At least one reproducible deployment sample is provided
- [ ] Integration and error-path tests are included
- [ ] Documentation clearly lists supported hardware, models, APIs, metrics, routing policies, and known limitations

### Area

Runtime

items.title: [cake deslop] cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell + cake_kimi_k3_mla (2): drop dead selectors, merge sm_103a copies, fold clones, decide exact shapes
items.author: yyihuang
items.body_excerpt:
**Background.** `csrc/cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell` (added in #4557, page-64 handshake in #5547) and `csrc/cake_kimi_k3_mla` (added in #5552, regenerated in #5602/#5627) serve only `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(backend="cake")` on sm_100a/sm_103a. `"auto"` never resolves to Cake (`flashinfer/mla/_core.py:3830-3836`). `_core.py:4296-4390` sends the supported DENSE/TOPK dimension tuples to `trtllm_mla_blackwell_decode`, which has 10 domains × 2 arches = 20 JIT families over 16 device sources. It sends other requests to `run_cake_kimi_k3_mla_fp8_paged_attention`: FP8 only, kv_lora_rank 512, rope 64, page 64, with 10 programs × 2 arches. Both families are JIT-only, and every source is compiled by some module. At 3184bbea the trtllm dir is 37 files / 29,788 lines: 16 kernels (22,534 lines) and 20 bindings (7,252 lines, split 3,626/3,626 between `sm_100a/` and `sm_103a/`). The kimi dir is 22 files / 17,514 lines. The Python is 2,813 lines: `flashinfer/mla/cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell.py` 1,723, `flashinfer/mla/cake_kimi_k3_mla.py` 655 and `flashinfer/jit/cake_kimi_k3_mla.py` 435. In round 1, #5805 (closed by #5968, +9,817/−69,570) removed 5 of 8 exact-geometry CLC variants and the unsplit 64x16x1024 program. It kept the other per-shape programs, with measured removal costs, as "a maintainer decision", along with 4 per-arch device pairs and 20 per-arch bindings. #5776 (closed by #5871, +1,824/−20,648) merged the kimi SM100/SM103 copies and cached planning, but did not template the row-tile and reducer programs. #6126 (+1,237/−4,481) then regenerated all kimi programs for the E4M3 reference-drop fix and folded the wide kernel under 162 `__CUDA_ARCH__` guards. No PR has touched either dir since, and nothing was re-added. What remains is what those PRs chose to keep.

**Findings**
- **Dead selector and registry plumbing.** Each of the 20 trtllm bindings has exactly one `case 0:`, and `SelectVariant()` is only a positivity guard (e.g. `num_split > 1`). `SelectVariant`, the switch and the `RouteOf`/`route_of` export take 484 gross lines, about 352 net after collapsing them to guard + `Run`. `route_of`, `route_entry` and `ffi_entry` have 0 consumers: `gen_cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell_family` (`cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell.py:754-781`) reads only arch/binding/dependencies/compile_flags, and Python only calls `.run`. `FAMILIES` (126-705, 580 lines) holds 20 `arg_plan` copies, of which 5 are unique. `.pre-commit-config.yaml:46` still excludes `cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell/generated/`, which #5968 deleted.
- **sm_103a bindings are copies.** With hashes and arch names neutralised, 9 of the 10 `sm_103a/*_binding.cu` files match their `sm_100a/` twins exactly. `clc_exact007826` differs in 4 lines: `dynamicSmemBytes` 231424 vs 230912, plus the matching `CakeSetMaxDynamicSmem` argument. 6 domains (vquarter, vhalf, bf16_tail, fp8_tail, fp8_p32, native split-8; 2,093 sm_103a lines) link the same device sources on both arches. The other 4 (clc, clc_exact007790, clc_exact007826, fp8_page64; 1,533 lines) link a different kernel per arch, so merging them needs a common `extern "C"` symbol. The loader already compiles each binding per arch with `_ARCH_NVCC_FLAGS`. These equivalence claims rest on text diffs; none has been SASS-checked yet.
- **Per-arch device pairs.** Four pairs are 88–97% identical: `clc` 74250d91/71fdced8 (raw diff 250 lines), `clc_exact007790` d7731e89/f2fc000e (183), `clc_exact007826` c343762a/d396fd37 (93) and the `fp8_page64` producer 03b4acda/88179fe5 (547). The sm_103a copies total 7,557 lines. #5968 kept the pairs because "traced schedules differ per architecture". However, its description calls the persistent CLC BF16 program "one source for both architectures", while `MODULES` (lines 71-78) still lists 74250d91 for sm_100a and 71fdced8 for sm_103a. The kimi wide kernel ea17187e (4,376 lines) already folds a larger difference under `__CUDA_ARCH__` guards.
- **Constant clones.**
  - vquarter 5a25f65a and vhalf 6a2644cd (1,349/1,361 lines) differ in 74 lines: `V_QUARTER`, loop bounds, split arithmetic, TMA bytes 8192/16384, one MMA instruction-descriptor immediate, and one vs two TMA loads per stage. Their 4 bindings are one 434-line text.
  - bf16_tail 6ba043a3 and fp8_tail d6056fe8 (197 lines each) differ in 8 lines: pointer dtype and `fp8_lut` decode.
  - Kimi `reduce_w4`/`w2`/`w1` (213/221/264 lines) differ in warps per row, vector width and accumulator sizes. Their 3 bindings (120 lines each) differ only by hash. #5776 asked for these to be templated; #5871 did not do it, and #6126 regenerated them unchanged.
  - Kimi row tiles rt16..rt96 (9,612 lines) share 41–75% of their text (ratios not rechecked) but are not pure constant clones.
- **Exact-shape programs.** 4 of 10 trtllm domains (14,128 lines) are reachable only on benchmark geometries. They are gated by `exact_route_candidate` (923-959) and `_host_kv_lens` (1211-1225); its `seq_lens.tolist()` (line 1224) is the only host sync in either family.
  - `mla_bf16_native_split8_pdl`: batch 1, KV 1024; 2,593 lines.
  - `mla_bf16_clc_exact007790`: batch 64, q_len 2, KV 8192; 4,134 lines.
  - `mla_bf16_clc_exact007826`: batch 512, q_len 16, KV 1024; 4,249 lines.
  - `mla_fp8_p32_qk_l2`: FP8, batch 1, q_len 2, KV 1024, page 32; 3,152 lines.

  Each has a runtime-shape fallback (vquarter, clc, clc and fp8_tail respectively). #5968 measured these removal costs: native split-KV +14% (B200) / +5% (B300) and +14% / +10% on its two rows; 007790 +1.3% / +4.4%; 007826 +1–2% / +9.8%; FP8 P32 227× (its fallback is the scalar tail). Under stream capture, `_host_kv_lens` returns None for an unseen tensor, so graph-captured decode reaches these programs only after an eager warm-up.
- **Silently ignored options.** `enable_pdl` (`cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell.py:1346`) is never read. PDL is hard-wired on in 5 of 10 trtllm domains (native_split8, clc, both exact CLC, fp8_page64) and in the 4 kimi reducer bindings, and off elsewhere. `skip_softmax_threshold_scale_fac

items.title: [Feature][Rubin] Export H4096 MegaMHC inference programs for GLM-5.3-Flash in vLLM (SM107)
items.author: yyihuang
items.body_excerpt:
### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing GitHub and Linear issues and related PRs. The H4096 training work and GB300 inference-fusion work below do not cover this specific export request.

### Problem

A vLLM user wants to run GLM-5.3-Flash with FlashInfer's MegaMHC inference kernel at **hidden size H=4096 on SM107 / Rubin**. Here H is the model hidden size, not an attention head dimension.

The current `flashinfer.mega_mhc.prepare_mega_mhc` backend exports only H5120 programs and admits SM100a / SM103a. Its generated route table has no H4096 program and its capability map has no SM107 entry:
[existing MegaMHC loader and program table](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/d4383335bae57d307edfcb58dce07bc78af2dece/flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_mega_mhc/mega_mhc.py).

### Requested outcome

Export and integrate H4096 MegaMHC inference programs usable from vLLM on SM107. Preserve the existing prepared-plan API where possible, including the post/pre mixing, projection, Sinkhorn, normalization and output contract needed by the caller.

The requested target is `sm_107a`. The requester also asked whether an `sm_100f` build could be used instead: explicitly establish compiler, instruction and binary/PTX compatibility on the target hardware before offering that route. A capability-map edit or target rename alone is not evidence of support.

### Target hardware

- Required: SM107 / Rubin (`sm_107a`).
- Possible alternative: `sm_100f` only if its suitability for the same SM107 deployment is demonstrated.
- Preserve the existing H5120 SM100a / SM103a paths.

### Inference engine

vLLM.

### Affected model or model family

GLM-5.3-Flash, hidden size 4096, four mHC residual streams.

### Workload and configuration

The existing API suggests the following H4096 shapes: `x[T,4096]`, `residual[T,4,4096]`, and projection `fn[24,16384]`. Confirm the deployed caller's dtypes, coefficient conventions, epsilon values, Sinkhorn settings, quantization and scale layouts before defining the supported contract.

Exact vLLM revision, checkpoint/quantization variant, CUDA version, device SM count, token-count distribution and parallelism were not supplied. In particular, the existing MegaMHC FP8-output contract and the NVFP4 serving model mentioned in #6892 should not be assumed interchangeable. Record the actual integration requirements and provide a minimal caller example.

### Current workaround

No working H4096 / SM107 export of `prepare_mega_mhc` has been identified. The H4096 training API in #6897 and the separate inference-fusion APIs under #6892 are related implementations to evaluate for reuse.

### Impact

Missing model/hardware coverage for the MegaMHC inference path; serving latency and integration usability.

### Acceptance criteria

- Deliver generated H4096 sources, dispatch/loader support and packaged artifacts that compile and execute on actual SM107 hardware with a documented toolchain.
- Match an independent reference and the vLLM caller's complete output contract, including residual/mixing values, normalized output and any required quantized outputs/scales.
- Test decode and prefill token counts, small/irregular counts and schedule boundaries, repeated calls with changed inputs, current-stream execution and CUDA Graph replay.
- Benchmark the full mHC call against the current vLLM path on the same GPU and inputs; report absolute latency, shapes, dtypes and workspace. Keep any model-level result separate from kernel timing.
- Preserve existing H5120 SM100/SM103 correctness and performance, and keep unsupported combinations explicit.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- #6892 (open, assigned to `nv-yunzheq`): GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 / vLLM fusion on GB300. Its open PRs are #6789 (`mhc_fused_post_pre`, H4096 SM103), #6790 (`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`, SM100/SM103 optimized path), and #6797 (all-reduce + mHC post/prenorm). Reuse applicable math, tests and integration knowledge; this issue tracks the remaining MegaMHC H4096 / SM107 export rather than a second implementation of those GB300 features.
- #6486, closed by merged #6897: H4096 forward/backward/checkpoint training on SM100/SM103/SM107 via `flashinfer.cake_mhc_train`; it does not add this inference export.
- #5523, #5955 and #6202: merged MegaMHC implementation, source consolidation and Sinkhorn optimization for the existing H5120 SM100/SM103 family.
- #4115: broader mHC pre and post/pre fusion request for DeepSeek V4.
- Parent kernel tracker: #4254.

Training/backward and a new distributed all-reduce implementation are outside this request.

items.title: [RFC]: Deterministic fault-injection harness for disaggregated serving
items.author: sylvesterkaczmarek

comments.author: codebreaker77
comments.body:
I'd like to help with a focused first slice of this RFC: a test-only scripted fault helper and an existing heartbeat regression migrated to use it.

Branch: https://github.com/codebreaker77/TensorRT-LLM/tree/test/18450-disagg-fault-harness

The helper targets a named async boundary, request/worker key and call occurrence. It provides explicit delay gates, dropped delivery, injected exceptions, a compact trace, and assertions for unused faults and still-active calls. It creates no background tasks and changes no production code or global clocks.

For a concrete existing consumer, test_heartbeat_survives_stalled_refresh_within_ttl now gates the first storage refresh instead of using a stall counter and long sleep. The worker's real per-attempt timeout cancels that call; retry succeeds. Original retry/deadline assertions remain, with an additional cancellation/retry trace and idle assertion.

Validation: 18 direct helper tests plus five watch-queue component checks and the migrated heartbeat regression pass on Windows Python 3.10 and Linux Python 3.12. The component checks execute unchanged production definitions and the actual regression function, while bypassing full package/native initialization. A temporary mutation removing the per-attempt timeout fails the regression as expected. Checked-in component tests retain normal production imports for supported CI; full-package collection has not been validated locally.

This initial slice does not provide virtual time, transport injection or full worker/transfer lifecycle coverage. The documented gate controls ordering only; the heartbeat test retains the real production timeout and clock.

Would this helper interface and first regression migration be a suitable initial contribution? Is the RFC author already working on the core fixture? I can adjust scope before requesting review.

comments.author: sylvesterkaczmarek
comments.body: This is a good first slice. I have not started a separate implementation of the fixture in this workstream. I checked the helper and ran its 18 isolated CPU tests: all passed. Please open a draft PR with the helper and one migrated heartbeat regression, keeping the no-virtual-time limitation explicit. The normal-import component and heartbeat tests still need to run in NVIDIA CI before claiming integration coverage.

items.title: [Performance]: copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDeviceKernel walks each long block-offset row with one CTA
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

`KVCacheManagerV2.copy_batch_block_offsets` launches `copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDeviceKernel` (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2Utils.cu`) once per manager per step. Its grid is `(num_pools, num_seqs)`: a single 128-thread CTA walks each whole row of block offsets, two `cp.async` loads deep, reading the pinned host table. For long-context pools the rows are long; at 32772 blocks per sequence, each CTA runs 64 sequential load iterations. The kernel is then latency bound, with a handful of CTAs on the whole GPU.

Measured on Rubin, Kimi K3 decode (target manager with 2 pools, draft manager with 1, 32772 blocks per sequence, 1 sequence): 28-33 µs per call, about 60 µs per decode step on the critical path between steps.

Proposal: add a third grid dimension that splits each row into tiles of 1024 offsets, one CTA each, keeping the per-element arithmetic and the read-at-execution-time semantics unchanged. A Triton prototype of exactly this tiling (same reads, same integer arithmetic, bitwise-equal output) took the call from 27.7 µs to 4.0 µs (2 pools) and from 27.0 µs to 3.6 µs (1 pool) in a microbenchmark. End to end on Rubin, TP8 across 2 nodes (MNNVL), single request, it reduced decode step time by 0.014-0.043 ms depending on context length, and 128K TTFT by 0.043 s.

PR to follow (draft; the C++ version still needs a GPU build and microbenchmark).

items.title: [Bug]: MPIPoolExecutor is not defined with ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF
items.author: xiaozhang8tuo
items.body_excerpt:
## Description

When TensorRT-LLM is built with `ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF`, the default
single-GPU launch path fails with:

    NameError: name 'MPIPoolExecutor' is not defined

## Cause

In `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/mpi_session.py`, `MPIPoolExecutor` is imported only
inside `if ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE:`, but
`GenerationExecutorProxy -> MpiPoolSession._start_mpi_pool` uses it on the
default startup path.

## Workaround

Set `TLLM_WORKER_USE_SINGLE_PROCESS=1`, which uses the single-process worker
path in `executor.py`.

## Environment

- TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc28
- Wheel built with
  `ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF;BUILD_NCCL_EXTENSIONS=OFF;ENABLE_UCX=OFF;BUILD_DEEP_EP=OFF`
- CUDA 13.2, Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- Single H200, PyTorch backend

## Notes

Follow-up requested in #20580, which fixes `mpi_allgather` for the same build
configuration. This issue is not addressed by that PR.

items.title: [BUG] cutlass_library does not emit grouped NVFP4 (ue4m3) block-scaled GEMM for SM120, although example 79d runs that kernel
items.author: waynehacking8
items.body_excerpt:
## Description

`GenerateSM120_TensorOp_fp4_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled` (`python/cutlass_library/generator.py`, ~L11441) skips grouped **NVFP4 (ue4m3)** block-scaled GEMM tile descriptions for SM120, behind this comment:

```python
# grouped schedules only support ue8m0 (MXF4); NVF4 (ue4m3) grouped requires
# NVF4-specific PtrArray schedule tags not yet available
```

That comment appears to be **stale**:

- `to_grouped_schedule()` (`python/cutlass_library/library.py`, L1051-1052) already maps
  `Nvf4TmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}Sm120 → PtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}`.
- Example **`examples/79_blackwell_geforce_gemm/79d_blackwell_geforce_nvfp4_grouped_gemm.cu`** instantiates exactly this kernel — `ArchTag = cutlass::arch::Sm120`, `e2m1` operands, `ue4m3` SF, `KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}` — and runs correctly.

Because the grouped schedules collapse to `PtrArray*`, `is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)` is `False` in the grouped branch, so only the `ue8m0` (MXF4) grouped tiles are emitted and the NVFP4 grouped tiles are dropped.

### Effect

The library / profiler / autotuner can select grouped **MXFP4** on SM120 but not grouped **NVFP4**, so frameworks running NVFP4 MoE on consumer Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090) don't get these grouped kernels and fall back to slower paths (related: #2800).

### Evidence (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, CUDA 13.0)

- Built + ran example 79d: both schedules `Disposition: Passed`, **303 / 253 TFLOPS**.
- Driving the grouped generator path directly (`GenerateSM120_TensorOp_fp4_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled(..., gemm_kind=GemmKind.GroupedBlockScaledUniversal3x)`):
  - today: 14 grouped fp4 ops, **0 NVFP4 (ue4m3) grouped**;
  - after adding an `is_grouped && ue4m3` clause: 28 ops, **14 NVFP4 grouped** (e.g. `cutlass3x_sm120_bstensorop_gemm_grouped_ue4m3xe2m1_ue4m3xe2m1_f32_void_f32_128x32x128_1x1x1_0_tnt_align32_warpspecialized_pingpong`).

### Proposed fix

In the grouped branch, key on the SF type instead of `is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)` (which only matches the non-grouped Sm120 tags):

```diff
         if (is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue8m0) or \
+           (is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue4m3) or \
            (not is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue4m3 and is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)) or \
            (not is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue8m0 and not is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)):
```

Happy to send this as a PR (with the stale comment corrected). I verified emission (0 → 14) and the kernel template via example 79d, but did not run a full `cutlass_profiler` build of all emitted tile variants locally — worth confirming in CI that every tile compiles (some SM120 tiles may hit Stages≥2 constraints; if so they can be pruned in the same clause).

cc @depaulmillz — this is the SM12x grouped / block-scaled generator area.

items.author: 0z5a
items.body_excerpt:
## Report incorrect documentation

**Location:** [TVM FFI compilation guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/91843b71d90737e0a9b86f7d9df213cff5a3526f/media/docs/pythonDSL/guides/tvm_ffi_compilation.rst), at the v4.8.1 source revision.

**Problems:** Following the examples encounters several independent failures:

- The tuple example annotates its argument with `Tuple` without importing it.
- The keyword-argument example uses `cutlass.Float32` without importing `cutlass`.
- The intentionally invalid CUDA launch raises a DSL CUDA diagnostic that is not caught by the shown `except RuntimeError`.
- The keyword-argument export example omits `inspect` and `subprocess` imports. Its `load_module("./add_constant.so")` also selects the default CuTe ABI for a TVM FFI export; it needs `enable_tvm_ffi=True`.

**Verification:** Executed 12 extracted guide cases with CuTe DSL 4.8.1 in GH200 and H100 environments. Each case includes earlier guide definitions where needed and explicitly invokes functions defined by the guide. On both machines the original examples give 8 passes and 4 failures. With the imports, exception type and loader ABI corrected, all 12 pass, including numerical and expected-error checks. An additional GH200 check with imports repaired still fails at the export loader until the TVM FFI flag is supplied.

**Suggested fix:** Add the imports, catch `DSLCudaRuntimeError` in the invalid-launch example, and load the TVM FFI export with its matching ABI. This is a guide correction; no runtime change is needed.

items.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
items.author: jhsmith409
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micro-kernel
cache key.

Measured first-hit compile costs (RTX PRO 6000, synthetic MoE E=32/topk=4 driving
`B12xMoEWrapper.run` exactly as vLLM's `FlashInferB12xExperts` does):

| kernel path | first hit | subsequent (same key) |
|---|---|---|
| dynamic (m-independent key) | ~40 s | 1–3 ms |
| micro m=1 | 14.9 s | ms |
| micro m=2 | 15.2 s | ms |
| micro m=64 | 18.3 s | ms |

Production symptom: vllm#47458 — py-spy captured 16 consecutive samples over 8.35 s pinned
in `b12x_fused_moe (flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py:166)` during a live
~17.5 s engine-wide stall; `perf` showed `_cutlass_ir.cpython-312.so` frames present only
during stalls.

## Why this deserves a disk layer even after #3836

#3836 stops *rekeying* (recompiles within one process). But serving engines restart —
deploys, config changes, crash recovery, autoscaling — and each fresh process re-pays the
entire compile set: ~40 s dynamic + 15–18 s per small-shape class. For a model like
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B this is 1–2 minutes of mid-serving stalls per engine lifetime that a
disk cache would reduce to milliseconds. The artifacts are deterministic products of
(kernel source, shape/config tuple, DSL version, arch) — exactly what file caches are for.

## Suggested fix directions

Either would resolve it; the first is contained entirely in flashinfer:

1. **flashinfer grows its own disk layer for sm12x MoE kernels**: serialize the compiled
   artifact keyed by the existing `cache_key` tuples + flashinfer version +
   nvidia-cutlass-dsl version + SM arch, under `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_DIR` (or a new env),
   loading into `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE` on miss. The DSL's own
   `compile_and_cache` machinery demonstrates the artifact is serializable (the implicit
   path already writes/reads `.mlir` + compiled objects).
2. **Upstream: nvidia-cutlass-dsl honors its file cache under explicit `cute.compile`**
   (stop hardcoding `no_cache=True`, or add an opt-in kwarg flashinfer can pass).

A third, cheaper-but-partial option is an official warm-up API (the attempt in
vllm#47599 was closed unmerged): it moves the cost to boot but still re-pays it every
process start, and needs the largest-workspace-first ordering to avoid #3836 rekeying —
a disk cache composes with, rather than replaces, that.

## Cross-references

- vllm#47458 — serving-stall report this splits from (mechanism established in-thread by
  @waynehacking8; py-spy confirmation by me)
- flashinfer#3836 — the workspace-rekeying half (open)

items.title: Use SymInt instead of sympy.Expr uniformly in Inductor
items.author: ezyang
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Sympy passes sympy.Expr around directly but this makes a lot of manipulations annoying. For example,

```
V.graph.sizevars.guard_equals(sympy_product(old_size), sympy_product(new_size))
```

This doesn't install a deferred runtime assert when there are unbacked SymInts. If you had done the equivalent torch._check it would have done so.

Similarly, guard size oblivious has to be spelled specially

```
V.graph.sizevars.shape_env.evaluate_expr(
                sympy.Eq(old_size[i], 1), size_oblivious=True
            )
```

See also @bdhirsh's recent PR https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/136670

So how can we do this port? It would be nice to do it incrementally.

* As a start, let's have easy APIs for converting between sympy.Expr and SymInt
* A good start is in lowering.py; specifically, without changing the external facing API, let's write a decorator that wraps sympy.Expr into SymInt on entry to the lowering function, and unwraps them when they exit. 
* We also want to change IR nodes so that they accept SymInt instead of sympy.Expr... maybe there can be some intermediate state where they accept either
* More typing in Inductor would help do the porting without having to do a full test suite run...

items.title: [cuDNN][SDPA] SM 10.7 + cuDNN < 9.25: cuDNN is preferred but no forward plan builds; retrying the same shape segfaults (null MHAGraphCache entry)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related problems on a Vera Rubin GPU (compute capability 10.7) with torch 2.14.0+cu132 and its bundled cuDNN 9.24.0.

**1. Default SDPA dispatch fails instead of falling back.** `check_prefer_cudnn_attention()` returns true for all `major == 10` devices in CUDA >= 13 builds, so cuDNN is tried first. On SM 10.7, cuDNN 9.24's heuristics return only runtime-compiled engines (`eng10_k24=1_k27=0_k38=0_k40=3_k41=2` and three `eng8` configs). Each one fails in `cudnnBackendFinalize` with `CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR_COMPILATION_FAILED: Encountered runtime kernel compilation failure at: compilationResult != NVRTC_SUCCESS`. The NVRTC version does not matter: 13.2 from the wheel and 13.4.92 give the same failure. Minimal repro:

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
q = torch.randn(1, 16, 1024, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q)
# RuntimeError: cuDNN Frontend error: [cudnn_frontend] Error: No valid execution plans built.
```

Every shape that dispatches to cuDNN fails: seq len 256-8192, head_dim 32/64/128, bf16 and fp16, contiguous or strided. Flash, mem-efficient and math all work on the same inputs. cuDNN 9.25.1.1, 9.26.1.1 and 9.27.0.42 (loaded into the same process instead of 9.24) select `eng18`, which builds and runs correctly, and is about 3.4x faster than flash for `[1, 16, 8192, 64]`.

There is already an `is_unsupported_sm107` guard (`cudnn_version <= 92500`) in `check_cudnn_hardware_support`, but it only limits head_dim to 128. It does not stop cuDNN from being selected for the common head dims. Suggested fix: on SM 10.7 with cuDNN < 9.25, either reject cuDNN in `check_cudnn_hardware_support` / `check_prefer_cudnn_attention`, or extend the existing guard to all head dims.

**2. Calling again with the same shape after the failure segfaults.**

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
q = torch.randn(1, 16, 1024, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
for _ in range(2):
    try:
        F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(e)
# 1st call: RuntimeError (above); 2nd call: Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault
```

This also happens under `sdpa_kernel([SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION])`. The cause is in `aten/src/ATen/native/cudnn/MHA.cpp` (release/2.14 and main): `run_cudnn_SDP_fprop` does `getMHAGraphCache_().try_emplace(key, nullptr)` and then assigns `cache_it->second = build_graph(...)`. When `build_graph` throws, the `nullptr` entry stays in the cache. The next call with the same key takes the cache-hit path and dereferences `*cache_it->second`. The backward path (`run_cudnn_SDP_bprop`) uses the same `try_emplace(key, nullptr)` pattern. Fix: erase the entry when the build throws, or insert only after a successful build.

Problem 1 only affects builds that still ship cuDNN < 9.25 (e.g. the 2.14.x cu13 wheels with cuDNN 9.24). Problem 2 does not depend on the cuDNN version: any graph build failure poisons the cache for that shape, turning a recoverable exception into a crash. Downstream, this breaks applications that call SDPA on SM 10.7 (for example the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder in TensorRT-LLM), and it means they cannot work around problem 1 with try/except.

Related (not duplicates): #190949 (d=256 cuDNN support surface on sm107, which added `is_unsupported_sm107`), #190388 (LRU bound for `MHAGraphCache`, does not touch the null-entry case), #193247 (CUDA 13.4 wheels moved to cuDNN 9.25).

### Versions

torch 2.14.0+cu132 (git 08187d9e0f), cuDNN 9.24.0 (runtime and compile time), cudnn-frontend 1.26 (bundled), CUDA 13.2 wheel runtime, also reproduced with NVRTC 13.4.92. GPU: Vera Rubin, compute capability 10.7. aarch64.

items.title: [Data] Ray Data CBO (Cost-Based Optimizer) Design
items.author: kaori-seasons
items.body_excerpt:
### Description

## 1. Background and Motivation

### 1.1 Problem Statement

Ray Data currently uses a purely Rule-Based Optimizer (RBO). All optimization rules are executed in a fixed topological order, with no awareness of data statistical characteristics. This means the following critical parameters can only be set manually by engineers:

- **Reservation ratio** `op_resource_reservation_ratio`: Controls the memory reservation proportion for each operator, defaults to 0.5
- **Shuffle partition count** `num_partitions`: Number of partitions for Join/Sort/Repartition
- **Read parallelism**: Number of output blocks for the Read operator

```python
# Engineer A's config (long pipeline + GPU mix)
ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.7

# Engineer B's config (short pipeline + batch inference)
ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.2

# Engineer C's config (doesn't know what to set, uses default 0.5)
ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.5

# But 0.5 may be too high or too low, depending on:
# - How many operators are in the pipeline?
# - What is the data amplification/reduction ratio for each operator?
# - Are there GPU operators?
# - Are there AllToAll (Sort/Shuffle) operators?
# - How severe is the data skew?
```

**Core contradiction**: This information can be derived from data statistical characteristics before execution, but the current RBO is entirely unable to leverage it.

### 1.2 Quantified Impact

| Scenario | Issue with default R=0.5 | Ideal R value |
|----------|--------------------------|---------------|
| Long pipeline (6 operators) + GPU | Insufficient reservation, GPU operators frequently backpressured | 0.6~0.7 |
| Short pipeline (2 operators) + batch inference | Over-reservation, resources idle and wasted | 0.2~0.3 |
| Sort pipeline (AllToAll) | Upstream reservation meaningless (memory limit lifted) | 0.2~0.3 |
| Single-operator-dominated pipeline | Reservation for other operators meaningless | 0.1~0.2 |

### 1.3 Design Goals

This proposal designs a CBO (Cost-Based Optimizer) for Ray Data, addressing the following problems:

1. **Auto-derive `reservation_ratio`**: Based on data statistics and cost model, eliminating manual tuning
2. **Auto-derive `num_partitions`**: Adapt Join/Shuffle partition counts to data volume
3. **Automatic Join reordering**: Automatically place the smaller table on the build side for INNER JOINs
4. **Runtime feedback**: Use runtime metrics from previous executions to correct compile-time estimates

### 1.4 Non-Goals (Scope Out)

- **SQL optimization**: No subquery unnesting, view rewriting, or other SQL-layer optimizations
- **Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)**: No dynamic changes to execution plan topology during execution
- **Multi-tenant resource isolation**: No cross-pipeline resource contention awareness
- **Column statistics for non-Parquet data sources**: CSV/JSON and other data sources do not support column-level statistics for now

---

## 2. Constraints

### 2.1 Architectural Constraints

**C-1: Must use existing Rule/Optimizer/Ruleset interfaces**

```python
# Source path: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/interfaces/optimizer.py

class Rule:
    def apply(self, plan: Plan) -> Plan:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @classmethod
    def dependencies(cls) -> List[Type["Rule"]]:
        return []  # Pre-dependencies

    @classmethod
    def dependents(cls) -> List[Type["Rule"]]:
        return []  # Post-dependents

class Optimizer:
    def optimize(self, plan: Plan) -> Plan:
        previous_plan = plan
        while True:
            for rule in self.rules:
                plan = rule.apply(plan)
            if plan.dag.dag_str == previous_plan.dag.dag_str:
                break  # Converged
            previous_plan = plan
        return plan
```

All CBO rules must implement the `Rule` interface and register via `Ruleset`. Bypassing the `Optimizer.optimize()` convergence loop is not allowed.

**C-2: Three-phase execution pipeline must not be changed**

```python
# Source path: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/optimizers.py

def get_execution_plan(logical_plan: LogicalPlan) -> PhysicalPlan:
    # 1. Logical optimization
    optimized_logical_plan = LogicalOptimizer().optimize(logical_plan)
    # 2. Plan conversion
    physical_plan = create_planner().plan(optimized_logical_plan)
    # 3. Physical optimization
    return PhysicalOptimizer().optimize(physical_plan)
```

CBO statistics propagation rules should be registered in the logical optimization phase; CBO parameter derivation rules should be registered in the physical optimization phase.

**C-3: `ReservationOpResourceAllocator` reservation model must not be changed**

```
Per-operator reservation = M × R / N
where M = total resources, R = reservation_ratio, N = number of active operators
```

CBO can only modify the global `R` value (`DataContext.op_resource_reservation_ratio`); it cannot change the reservation formula itself. Half of the reservation goes to internal buffers, half to outputs.

### 2.2 Compatibility Constraints

**C-4: Backward compatible — user-explicit settings take priority**

CBO-derived values only take effect when the user has **not explicitly set** them. A `_user_set_reservation_ratio` flag needs to be introduced in `DataContext` to distinguish "user intentionally set 0.5" from "used the default 0.5".

> Currently there is no such flag in `DataContext` (`grep _user_set` returns empty); it needs to be added.

**C-5: Must safely fall back when statistics are unavailable**

For non-Parquet data sources, custom Datasources, encrypted data, etc., statistics may be entirely unavailable. CBO must fall back to existing RBO behavior without producing worse results.

**C-6: Expressions API is in Alpha stage**

Ray Data's expression system (`BinaryExpr`, `ColumnExpr`, `LiteralExpr`, etc.) is annotated with `@DeveloperAPI(stability="alpha")`, and the interface may change. Selectivity estimation logic must be loosely coupled with the Expressions API.

### 2.3 Performa

items.title: [Core/Auth] Enable token authentication by default for all clusters in Ray 2.61
items.author: MortalHappiness
items.body_excerpt:
Since Ray 2.59, token authentication is on by default only for local clusters. Every other cluster (started by hand, by `ray up` and the autoscaler, by KubeRay, or by the Anyscale platform) still runs with auth disabled, so anyone who can reach its ports can run arbitrary code. Ray 2.61 makes token auth the default for every cluster. `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` stays the opt-out.

Goals:

- Every newly started cluster, local or remote, has token auth on unless the user sets `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled`.
- A bare `ray.init()`, C++ and Java drivers that start their own local cluster, and `ray.cluster_utils.Cluster()` stay zero-config; `ray start --head` needs a token created first. Every tool in this repo works with auth on.
- The local-cluster special cases are deleted, with no dead branches left.

Design:

- `AUTH_MODE` defaults to `"token"` in `src/ray/common/ray_config_def.h`. The local-cluster special cases added in #64755, #66467 and #66778 are deleted, since every path is already in token mode.
- `ray start --head` never creates a token; with none, it fails with an error that says to run `ray get-auth-token --generate` and put the token on every node. A bare `ray.init()`, `ray.cluster_utils.Cluster()` and C++/Java drivers that start their own cluster create a missing one. Connecting nodes and clients never create one; without a token they fail fast with an error that names `ray get-auth-token` and the `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` opt-out.
- The token never goes on a command line. `ray up` ships it to the head node as a file mount, and the head ships it to the worker nodes it launches. `image_uri`/`container` workers get it as a read-only file mount when the node's token is a file, and by name from podman's environment when the node has it only in `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- A client in token mode talking to a cluster that opted out gets an error instead of silent success. gRPC servers in disabled mode reject requests that carry a token. HTTP clients check `GET /api/authentication_mode` instead, because reverse proxies in front of a disabled dashboard can send their own `Authorization` header (the former `kuberay-auth.md` guide set one up with kube-rbac-proxy; also ray-project/kuberay#1824, #42606).
- Ray's Prometheus metrics endpoints (nodes, autoscaler, dashboard head) require the token when auth is on. `ray metrics launch-prometheus` puts the token inline in its own config when `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set, and otherwise points it at `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH` or `~/.ray/auth_token`. The dashboard's template config for users' own Prometheus never gets the token. Setting `RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS=1` serves every Ray metrics endpoint without the token while auth still protects everything else.


How users use it in 2.61. Every sub-issue PR must keep these flows working as shown:

1. Local development. A bare `ray.init()` needs no setup: it connects to the running local cluster if there is one, and otherwise starts a new one and creates `~/.ray/auth_token` if it is missing. Before `ray start --head`, create the token once; everything in the same HOME then reads it.

```bash
ray get-auth-token --generate        # once; creates ~/.ray/auth_token if missing
ray start --head
ray start --address=127.0.0.1:6379   # a second node on the same machine
python -c "import ray; ray.init()"   # a driver
```

Without a token, `ray start --head` fails at once, before starting anything, with an error that says to run `ray get-auth-token --generate` and put the token on every node. C++ and Java drivers that start their own cluster, and `ray.cluster_utils.Cluster()`, create the token themselves.

2. A cluster built by hand across machines. The token file must be copied from the head to each machine; the token never goes on a command line.

```bash
# head machine
ray get-auth-token --generate
ray start --head
# worker machine, after the head's ~/.ray/auth_token is copied here
ray start --address=<head-ip>:6379
```

Without the copy, `ray start --address` fails at once with an error that says to run `ray get-auth-token` on the head and copy the token.

3. `ray up`. No token steps: `ray up` creates the token on the operator's machine if needed and ships it to the head node. The head ships it to every worker node it launches, including ones the autoscaler adds later.

```bash
ray up cluster.yaml
ray dashboard cluster.yaml &
ray job submit --address http://127.0.0.1:8265 -- python script.py
```

4. A client on another machine. Clients on the head machine, or on the machine that ran `ray up`, already have the token. Any other machine needs the token file copied to it.

```bash
# after the head's ~/.ray/auth_token is copied to this machine
ray job submit --address http://<head-ip>:8265 -- python script.py
```

`RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH` is only needed when the token file lives somewhere other than `~/.ray/auth_token`.

5. Opting out. Every node and every client sets `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled`. The head logs a warning that auth is disabled.

```bash
RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled ray start --head
RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled ray start --address=<head-ip>:6379
RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled ray job submit --address http://<head-ip>:8265 -- python script.py
```

A node or client that leaves out `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` fails with an error telling it to set it: AuthModeMismatch if it has a token, the missing-token error if it doesn't. For `ray up`, put `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` in the cluster YAML's start commands.

6. Mismatches never fall back to auth off. A worker or client with no token, a different token, or a different auth mode than the head fails right away with an error that names the fix. It does not hang or connect without auth.

7. Prometheus scraping. `ray metrics launch-prometheus` works with no change. With `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` set, it writes the token into its own config (`./prometheus-<version>.linux-amd64/ray_prometheus.yml`, mode 0600); otherwise the config reads `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH` or `~/.ray/auth_token`. items.title: [Core] Keep job env_vars values off podman's command line in image_uri and container runtime envs
items.author: MortalHappiness
items.body_excerpt:
### Description

For `image_uri` and `container` runtime envs, `RuntimeEnvContext._exec_container_worker` in `python/ray/_private/runtime_env/context.py` passes the job's `env_vars` to podman as `--env NAME=VALUE`. The values stay in podman's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for the worker's whole lifetime, so they show in `ps` and in the dashboard's process view. The dashboard reporter only redacts `--serialized-runtime-env-context=`. `runtime_env={"image_uri": ..., "env_vars": {"DB_PASSWORD": "..."}}` puts `--env DB_PASSWORD=...` on that command line. This predates #66975 (master put the same values in its `bash -c` string), and `.claude/rules/security.md` says `env_vars` values must not go on process command lines.

The proposed fix is to pass the job's values through `--env-file=/dev/fd/N`, where N is an inherited `os.memfd_create` fd holding `NAME=VALUE` lines. The env file goes before the by-name `RAY_*` `--env` flags and `run_options`, so a later `--env` still wins as it does now. An env file can't hold a newline in a value, so runtime env setup should reject such a value with an error that names the variable. We also need to check that rootless podman still reads the fd after it re-execs itself.

### Use case

Follow-up to #66975. Jobs pass credentials through `env_vars`, and other local users and dashboard viewers shouldn't see them on a container worker's command line.

items.title: Illegal memory access in triton kernel and non-determinism codegen
items.author: xw285cornell
items.body_excerpt:
Hi team, we seem to identified an issue that triton is generating non-deterministic codegen results, and in certain cases (small chances) it seems to have illegal memory access due to out of bound access in shared memory. 
The triton code is fairly simple (shown below). We run the code many times (disabled pytorch's codegen cache) and it seems it produced different shared memory: 
Most of times: 
{"name": "triton__0d1d2d3d4", "shared": 2560, "num_warps": 4, "num_stages": 1}
Sometimes: 
{"name": "triton__0d1d2d3d4", "shared": 544, "num_warps": 4, "num_stages": 1}

So sometimes it only asks for 544 bytes for shared memory space which might lead to out of bound access to shared mem. We checked and ttir is the same across the two runs, but llir is different. Wondering if you can shed some lights on this (and whether the codegen is deterministic. Also this is still on llvm IR - not sure if it repros in MLIR. 

```
from torch._inductor.triton_ops.autotune import pointwise

@pointwise(
    size_hints=[262144, 64],
    tile_hint=TileHint.DEFAULT,
    filename="notebook",
    meta={
        "signature": {0: "*bf16", 1: "*fp32", 2: "*bf16", 3: "i32", 4: "i32"},
        "device": 0,
        "constants": {},
        "mutated_arg_names": [],
        "configs": [instance_descriptor(divisible_by_16=(0, 1, 2, 3), equal_to_1=())],
    },
)
@triton.jit
def triton_(
    in_ptr0,
    in_ptr1,
    out_ptr0,
    xnumel,
    ynumel,
    XBLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    YBLOCK: tl.constexpr,
):
    xnumel = 262144
    ynumel = 62
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:, None]
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    yoffset = tl.program_id(1) * YBLOCK
    yindex = yoffset + tl.arange(0, YBLOCK)[None, :]
    ymask = yindex < ynumel
    x0 = xindex % 512
    x1 = xindex // 512
    y2 = yindex
    x3 = xindex
    tmp0 = tl.load(
        in_ptr0
        + (
            512
            + x0
            + (1536 * x1)
            + (786432 * y2)
            + (786432 * (((x0 + (512 * x1)) // 262144)))
        ),
        xmask & ymask,
    ).to(tl.float32)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + (512 + x0), xmask)
    tmp2 = tmp1.to(tl.float32)
    tmp3 = tmp0 + tmp2
    tmp4 = 2.8284271247461903
    tmp5 = tmp3 / tmp4
    tl.store(
        out_ptr0 + (y2 + (62 * x3) + tl.zeros([XBLOCK, YBLOCK], tl.int32)),
        tmp5,
        xmask & ymask,
    )
```

items.title: [BUG] CuTe DSL: export_to_c fails for a --gpu-arch other than the current GPU's
items.author: hwanseoc
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CuTe DSL

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

`export_to_c` fails on the plain C path (no `--enable-tvm-ffi`) when the function was compiled for a different arch than the current GPU. For example, `--gpu-arch sm_90a` on a B200:

```text
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ _cuKernelGetAttribute, _cudaDeviceGetAttribute, _cudaFuncSetAttribute, _cudaGetDevice, _cudaKernelSetAttributeForDevice, _cudaLaunchKernelEx, _cudaLibraryGetKernel, _cudaLibraryLoadData ]
error: Error dumping object file: Failed to dump object file with PIC relocation
```

The same export works for the native arch, and it also works if I load the runtime libraries `RTLD_GLOBAL` first. My guess is that no execution engine gets built for an arch the GPU can't run, so `libcute_dsl_runtime.so` never gets loaded before the object dump.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

```python
import ctypes, sys, tempfile

import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream


@cute.kernel
def noop_kernel(x: cutlass.Int32):
    pass


@cute.jit
def noop(x: cutlass.Int32, stream: cuda.CUstream):
    noop_kernel(x).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(32, 1, 1), stream=stream)


if "--preload" in sys.argv:
    for lib in cute.runtime.find_runtime_libraries(enable_tvm_ffi=False):
        ctypes.CDLL(lib, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
fn = cute.compile(noop, cutlass.Int32(0), make_fake_stream(), options="--gpu-arch sm_90a")
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    fn.export_to_c(tmp, "noop", function_prefix="noop")
print(f"cutlass-dsl {cutlass.__version__}: exported", flush=True)
```

```console
$ python repro.py
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ _cuKernelGetAttribute, ... ]
$ python repro.py --preload
cutlass-dsl 4.8.0: exported
```

**Expected behavior**

`export_to_c` works for any `--gpu-arch` the compiler accepts, with no manual preloading.

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: Bare-metal
 - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 and 4.7.0 (cu13), cuda-python 13.4.1
 - B200, driver 580.159.03, Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12

**Additional context**

#2859 had the same error on the TVM-FFI path and was fixed in 4.3.3; the TVM-FFI path does export cross-arch now. The plain C path still fails. Workaround: preload `cute.runtime.find_runtime_libraries()` with `RTLD_GLOBAL`.

items.title: [BUG] SM90 TMA GEMM mainloops rely on elect_one_sync() electing lane 0 (TMA issuer vs. PipelineTmaAsync is_leader)
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CUTLASS C++

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

**Summary.** Most SM90 TMA GEMM mainloop collectives work only if `elect.sync` elects lane 0, because two threads are chosen by different rules: the TMA issuer is the elected lane, while the producer's arrival comes from warp-group thread 0. PTX does not say which lane `elect.sync` elects, and if another lane were elected the kernel would hang. We suggest deriving the leader from the election in the mainloop warp, as in-tree code already does elsewhere.

Paths and lines are at main `0b55a2f`.

#### Evidence

**TMA issuer.** These collectives call `producer_acquire` and issue the TMA copies only inside `if (lane_predicate)`, where `lane_predicate = cute::elect_one_sync()`, that is, `elect.sync` with a full mask:

| Collective (`include/cutlass/gemm/collective/`) | elect / `producer_acquire` lines |
|---|---|
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 320 / 374 |
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 318 / 372 |
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized.hpp` | 401 / 457 |
| `sm90_sparse_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 415 / 458 |
| `sm90_sparse_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 426 / 469 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 370 / 425 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 368 / 422 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8_blockwise_scaling.hpp` | 463 / 543 |

The non-warp-specialized `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp` (lines 365 and 504) and the SM90 implicit-GEMM conv collective (`conv/collective/sm90_implicit_gemm_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp:558–559, 612`) have the same pattern.

**Producer arrival.** `PipelineTmaAsync::producer_acquire` performs `arrive_and_expect_tx` only when `params_.is_leader` is set (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:533–535`, and 555–557 in the token overload). This arrival is the stage's only producer arrival. The kernels set `is_leader = warp_group_thread_idx == 0`:
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:324`;
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_cooperative.hpp:471`;
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_pingpong.hpp:463`;
- the array cooperative and pingpong kernels, lines 522 and 531;
- `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp:334`.

The mainloop warp is warp 0 of the producer warp group, so warp-group thread 0 is its lane 0.

#### Cause

PTX ISA 9.4 (§9.7.15.15, `elect.sync`) promises only that the election is deterministic, with the same leader for the same `membermask` every time. It does not say which lane. If another lane were elected:
- that lane would call `producer_acquire` without being the leader, so nothing arrives on the full barrier;
- lane 0 would not enter the `if` at all;
- the TMA's complete-tx would only drive the transaction count negative.

The phase would never complete. Consumers would block in `consumer_wait`, then the producer in `producer_acquire` once every stage is used.

#### Suggested fix

Precedents for deriving the leader from the election:
- on the same `PipelineTmaAsync`, `examples/88_hopper_fmha/kernel/fmha_kernel_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:205, 210` and `sm120_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_cooperative_asymmetric_dma.hpp:443, 448`;
- in the SM100 kernels, e.g. `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:465`.

For the SM90 kernels, that would be:

```cpp
mainloop_pipeline_params.is_leader =
    warp_group_role == WarpGroupRole::Producer &&
    producer_warp_role == ProducerWarpRole::Mainloop && lane_predicate;
```

Restrict it to the mainloop warp. The `MainloopAux` warp in the blockwise kernels also has the Producer role and calls `producer_acquire` from all lanes. Giving it a leader would add a second `arrive_and_expect_tx` per stage.

This works because the kernel's `elect_one_sync()` and the collective's later one use the same full mask, and PTX guarantees the same leader for the same mask. Two more changes go with it:
- `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp` would need `lane_predicate` computed before `is_leader` is set;
- the debug-build `brkpt` checks in `producer_acquire` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:542–544` and 564–566), which fire when the leader is not lane 0, would need to go. They already assume lane 0 for the FMHA and SM120 kernels above.

The alternative is to gate the TMA issue in each affected collective on lane 0 instead of `elect_one_sync()`.

#### Scope

- Unaffected: some collectives call `producer_acquire` from all 32 lanes and issue TMA only from the elected lane, so lane 0 always arrives:
  - the mixed-input collectives (`sm90_mma_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized_mixed_input.hpp:684/694`, and the array variant at 774/784);
  - the non-array FP8 blockwise collective (577/587–588).

  The epilogue's TMA loads are also unaffected, because one elected lane both posts the expect-tx and issues the copy.
- Current hardware: the kernels run today, so current hardware evidently elects lane 0 here. The code also states that intent:
  - `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp:356` says "Set predicate for the lowest lane_id in the warp";
  - `sm90_pipeline.hpp:286` says "We have exactly one thread elected in the Producer as the 'leader'";
  - CuTe's fallback without `elect.sync` returns `(threadIdx.x % 32) == 0` (`include/cute/arch/cluster_sm90.hpp:197`).

#### Why there is no PR

The fix can go in the kernels (`is_leader` from the election) or in each affected collective (TMA issue gated on lane 0), so we'd rather follow your preference than guess. Tell us which and we'll write the PR.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

Found by reading the source against the PTX ISA. There is no runtime reproduction.

**Expected behavior**

The lane that issues the TMA loads is the lane that arrives with the expected bytes.

**Environment details**

Source analysis; no runtime environment involved. Hopper (sm_90a).

items.title: [DOC] Dynamic-layout guide example uses incompatible singleton strides
items.author: 0z5a
items.body_excerpt:
## Report incorrect documentation

**Location:** [Framework integration guide, dynamic-layout code example](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/91843b71d90737e0a9b86f7d9df213cff5a3526f/media/docs/pythonDSL/guides/framework_integration.rst), at the v4.8.1 source revision.

**Problem and reproduction:** The example assumes that singleton dimensions of `b` have stride 1, but the shown PyTorch construction retains stride 4:

```python
import torch
from cutlass.cute.runtime import from_dlpack

b = torch.empty(32, 1, 1, 1, 4).permute(3, 4, 1, 0, 2)
print(b.stride())  # (4, 1, 4, 4, 4)
from_dlpack(b).mark_layout_dynamic(leading_dim=0)
# Expected strides[leading_dim] == 1, but got 4
```

The same mismatch affects the later `leading_dim=2` example. The `t1` and `t2` examples also print `t2` and `t3`, respectively, before those variables have been defined.

**Verification:** Ran the six positive examples t0–t5 in a GH200 environment with the main editable core and torch 2.11.0, and an H100 environment with CuTe DSL 4.8.1 and torch 2.13.0. The original and a print-only repair fail at the stride check. Using explicit singleton strides and correcting the print variables makes all six layouts match the documented output in both environments. This checks tensor-layout metadata, not GPU kernel performance; deliberate-error snippets elsewhere in the guide are outside this report.

**Suggested fix:** Construct `b` with `torch.empty_strided((1, 4, 1, 32, 1), (1, 1, 1, 4, 1))`, and print the variables just defined.

items.title: [Store] Does Mooncake store plan to support awareness of layers, chunk ordering, and TP?
items.author: Hadigan
items.body_excerpt:
It looks like the current Mooncake store does not have awareness of layer granularity, chunk order (earlier vs. later chunks), or TP ranks. This can cause problems during cache eviction:

1. The store might evict KVs for only some layers, forcing prefill to recompute all layer KVs for those tokens.
2. The store might evict the KVs corresponding to the earliest chunk(s) of a token sequence, forcing prefill to recompute KVs for all chunks/tokens.
3. The store might evict KVs produced by some TP ranks, forcing all TP ranks to recompute KVs.

I think the Mooncake store should be aware of layers, chunk ordering, and TP. On eviction, it should evict a token’s KV caches for all layers and for all TP ranks together (i.e., keep KV state complete per token). 
From the chunk-order perspective, eviction policies should prefer removing KVs for later chunks first rather than evicting early-chunk KVs that make prefill expensive.
